Children under 5 perforate more often: short omentum.
Signs: Pain first epigastric/periumbilical, later right lower quadrant; vomiting comes after the pain.
McBurney tenderness, pain on hopping/cough; Rovsing's sign: pressing LIF hurts RIF.
Dx: Paediatric Appendicitis or Alvarado score: low discharge, high surgery, middle imaging.
First-line imaging is ultrasound: non-compressible tube >6 mm; CT only if inconclusive.
Rx: Analgesia given freely does not mask the diagnosis; IV fluids, antibiotics.
Laparoscopic appendicectomy.
Appendix mass → antibiotics first ± drainage, interval appendicectomy.

Def: Torsion: testis/ovary twists on its pedicle; cryptorchidism: testis not in scrotum.
Cause: Testis: bell-clapper deformity, usually bilateral; ovary: cyst or teratoma as lead weight.
Cryptorchidism: preterm (up to 30%) vs term 2-4%.
Patho: Torsion: veins occlude first → arterial failure → infarction.
Undescended testis → germ cells degenerate → infertility and testicular germ cell tumour.
Signs: Testis: sudden pain, vomiting, high-riding horizontal lie, cremasteric reflex absent.
Appendix testis torsion: blue dot sign, reflex preserved.
Ovary: sudden unilateral lower abdominal pain, vomiting, may mimic appendicitis.
Dx: Testicular torsion is clinical → theatre, not scan.
Ovary: US shows enlarged oedematous ovary; preserved Doppler does not exclude.
Bilateral impalpable testes → karyotype, exclude CAH.
Rx: Testis: explore within 6 hours (~90% salvage), detort, fix both sides.
Ovary: laparoscopic detorsion, untwisted and preserved even if dusky.
Cryptorchidism: refer by 3-6 months, orchidopexy at 6-18 months.

Def: Failed neural tube closure (week 4): cranial day 25, caudal day 28.
Anencephaly cranially; spina bifida (occulta, meningocele, myelomeningocele) caudally.
Cause: Folate deficiency (TMP-SMX in 1st trimester), previous NTD, valproate/carbamazepine, maternal diabetes, obesity.
Patho: Exposed placode damaged → deficits below the level.
Most myelomeningoceles: tethered cord → Chiari II → hydrocephalus.
Signs: Flaccid leg weakness, sensory loss, neurogenic bladder/bowel, club feet, scoliosis.
Hydrocephalus; stridor/apnoea from brainstem compression; latex allergy.
Dx: Raised maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein; ultrasound lemon (frontal bones) and banana (cerebellum) signs.
At birth: level, head circumference, fontanelle, hips, feet, bladder.
Rx: Prevent: folic acid 400 µg daily routinely, 5 mg if high risk.
Birth: moist sterile dressing, prone, no latex; close within 48 hours.
VP shunt/ETV; clean intermittent catheterisation, oxybutynin, physio.

Def: Perinatal oxygen deprivation causing encephalopathy (HIE), staged by Sarnat.
Cause: Abruption, cord prolapse, uterine rupture, shoulder dystocia, maternal hypotension.
Supports: sentinel event, Apgar ≤ 5 at 10 min, pH <7.0, base deficit ≥ 12-16.
Patho: Hypoxia → ATP fails → primary energy failure → oedema, excitotoxicity.
Latent phase 1-6 h (window) → secondary energy failure 6-72 h → neuronal death.
Diving reflex spares brain, heart, adrenals; kidneys, gut, liver suffer.
Signs: Mild: hyperalert, jittery; moderate: lethargy, hypotonia, seizures.
Severe: coma, flaccid, apnoea; multiorgan ATN, PPHN, DIC, hypoglycaemia.
Dx: Cord gas, aEEG (normalising by 24-48 h good).
MRI days 4-10: basal ganglia and thalamus injury = poor prognosis.
Apgar: Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, Respiration (10-point scale).
Rx: Cooling: moderate or severe HIE, babies ≥ 36 weeks.
33.5 °C for 72 hours, started within 6 hours; rewarm 0.5 °C per hour.
Normocapnia, avoid hyperthermia, restrict fluids; seizures → phenobarbital.

Def: Hydrocephalus: CSF accumulation with ventricular dilatation.
CP: essential criterion non-progressive, residual brain injury of developing brain.
Cause: Hydrocephalus: aqueduct stenosis, Chiari II, tumour, post-IVH/meningitis, congenital toxoplasmosis.
CP: antenatal (most), prematurity (PVL, IVH) strongest, HIE, kernicterus.
Patho: Obstruction or failed absorption → CSF builds → skull expands if sutures open.
Preterm IVH arises in the germinal matrix.
CP lesion static, picture evolves: hypotonia → spasticity, contractures.
Signs: Infant: head circumference crossing centiles, bulging fontanelle, sunsetting eyes.
CP: spastic commonest; dyskinetic (basal ganglia), ataxic (cerebellum).
Hand preference before 12 months suggests hemiplegia; loss of skills is not CP.
Dx: Hydrocephalus/IVH: cranial ultrasound (infant), MRI; bulging fontanelle + vomiting → brain imaging.
CP: standardised movement assessment + MRI; classify function by GMFCS.
Rx: Ventriculoperitoneal shunt or endoscopic third ventriculostomy; headache/vomiting/drowsiness = blockage.
CP: multidisciplinary physio/OT/SLT; baclofen, botulinum toxin, hip surveillance.

Def: Bacterial meningeal infection; brain abscess = walled-off pus in brain.
Cause: Neonates: Streptococcus agalactiae (GBS) and E. coli; Listeria.
Later: meningococcus, pneumococcus; abscess: ear/sinus spread, cyanotic CHD (right-to-left shunt bypasses lung filter).
Patho: Cytokines open BBB → protein elevated, glucose decreased, neutrophils.
Oedema, impaired CSF absorption → raised ICP.
Signs: Neck stiffness, Kernig, Brudzinski; infants: fever, irritability, bulging fontanelle.
Non-blanching rash → meningococcal sepsis.
Abscess: headache, focal signs, seizures; fever in only half.
Dx: LP: neutrophils >1000/µL, protein >1 g/L, CSF:blood glucose <0.4.
Raised ICP, shock, coagulopathy: delay LP, never delay antibiotics.
Abscess: ring-enhancing lesion; lumbar puncture contraindicated.
Rx: Antibiotics without delay: under 3 months cefotaxime + amoxicillin (covers Listeria); over 3 months ceftriaxone.
Dexamethasone over 3 months reduces hearing loss; test hearing within 4 weeks; contact prophylaxis.
Abscess: drain + IV antibiotics 4-8 weeks.

Def: Encephalitis = brain parenchyma inflammation; facial palsy = central (UMN) or peripheral (LMN).
Cause: Encephalitis: HSV-1 (key treatable cause), enterovirus, VZV; neonates HSV-2; anti-NMDAR, ADEM.
Facial palsy: Bell (exclusion), otitis, Lyme, Ramsay Hunt (VZV), hypertension, leukaemia.
Patho: HSV encephalitis typically affects the temporal lobe.
Upper face has bilateral cortical supply → forehead spared in central lesions.
Signs: Encephalitis: fever + altered behaviour/consciousness, seizures, focal signs.
Peripheral: whole half-face, can't close eye, taste loss; central: forehead sparing.
Bilateral palsy: Lyme, Guillain-Barre, leukaemia; Ramsay Hunt: ear vesicles.
Dx: LP: lymphocytic CSF, normal glucose; HSV PCR; MRI, EEG.
Every facial palsy: examine the ear, measure blood pressure; atypical course → image brain.
Rx: IV aciclovir on suspicion, 14-21 days (21 neonates); crystal-induced AKI risk.
ADEM methylprednisolone; anti-NMDAR in girls → search for ovarian teratoma.
Palsy: protect the eye, treat cause; prednisolone within 72 h.

Def: Neurocutaneous syndromes: skin + nervous system lesions (shared ectodermal origin).
Cause: NF1: neurofibromin, chromosome 17; NF2: merlin, chromosome 22 (AD).
TSC1/TSC2 (AD); Sturge-Weber: somatic GNAQ mutation, not inherited.
Patho: NF1: neurofibromin loss → Ras unchecked → neural crest tumours.
TSC: mTOR overactivity → hamartomas; SWS: leptomeningeal angioma → cortical ischaemia.
Signs: NF1: ≥ 6 café-au-lait macules, freckling, neurofibromas, optic glioma, Lisch nodules.
NF2: bilateral vestibular schwannomas; TSC: ash-leaf macules, angiofibromas, rhabdomyomas, infantile spasms.
SWS: V1 port-wine stain, seizures, hemiparesis, glaucoma.
Dx: NF1: two or more diagnostic features; annual eye checks.
TSC: Wood lamp for ash-leaf; infantile spasms show hypsarrhythmia (West syndrome).
SWS imaging: tram-track calcification.
Rx: NF1 plexiform neurofibroma: selumetinib (MEK inhibitor).
TSC spasms: first-line vigabatrin; SEGA: everolimus.
SWS: seizure control, low-dose aspirin, glaucoma follow-up, pulsed-dye laser.
